identity.name: Phil Selway
identity.summary: Radiohead's drummer since they were On a Friday at Abingdon School in 1985. He plays parts rather than chops, each written for its song: Creep's 'disciplined simplicity', Paranoid Android's cross-stick under eighths on the hat, There There's floor tom, Reckoner's ghost notes round the ride, 15 Step in 5/4 over a machine. 'Bits of soul drumming and hip-hop and even lighter jazz things all swimming around within my drumming,' he told Rhythm in 2001; he says he borrowed 'quite a bit from Stephen Morris's drumming', and from Kid A on learned to play the electronic parts on the kit. Also a solo singer and songwriter (Familial, 2010) and a Samaritans listener for seventeen years.

traditions.impact: Joy Division, the Clash and the Velvet Underground were his earliest influences; 'I have borrowed quite a bit from Stephen Morris's drumming'.
The ska revival 'a very formative scene'; The Beat's I Just Can't Stop It for his 13th birthday.
'Bits of soul drumming and hip-hop and even lighter jazz things' inside a rock band's beat, none 'a carbon copy'.

formative_events.event: Began drums and guitar at 15, 'for the social cachet and love of music'.
On a Friday formed at Abingdon School with Yorke, the Greenwoods and O'Brien.
Lessons with Bob Armstrong after a six-month break from the kit following OK Computer, 'to work on technique and get a better grasp of a lot of different styles'.

evidence.note: The year is the interview's "last year" (2000).

eras.label: Pablo Honey and The Bends
eras.context: A guitar band: Creep, then John Leckie's The Bends.

eras.label: OK Computer to Hail to the Thief
eras.context: Nigel Godrich's records: his playing cut into loops (Airbag, The National Anthem), machines on Kid A and Amnesiac, live drums back on Hail to the Thief.
defining_traits: the cross-stick and the toms in place of the snare
electronic parts played on the kit

eras.label: In Rainbows and after
eras.context: The kit over machines and loops; a second drummer on tour from 2011.

genres.name: Experimental rock
genres.notes: OK Computer to In Rainbows: loops, machines, odd meters.

swing.notes: Straight: every tab writes even eighths and sixteenths.

dynamics.balance: Often quiet, the cross-stick or the toms in place of the snare; full for the climaxes.

feel_profile.interaction: 'We give each other an awful lot of space to develop our parts' (OK Computer); from Kid A, playing machine parts on the kit.

hand_techniques.name: Cross-stick in place of the snare
hand_techniques.description: Paranoid Android's opening, There There, Creep's last chorus.

hand_techniques.name: Toms as the groove
hand_techniques.description: There There's floor tom in eighths, Bodysnatchers' bridge.

foot_techniques.name: The hat's foot on the beat
foot_techniques.description: Under the ride or the toms (Just, There There, Bodysnatchers).

coordination.notes: Odd meters: Paranoid Android's 7/8 groups, 15 Step in 5/4, 2 + 2 = 5's opening in 7/8.

devices_search.note: No device found: Paranoid Android's 7/8 bars and 15 Step's 5/4 are meters, not cross-rhythms; 15 Step's figure repeats every half bar inside the 5/4; Paranoid Android's slow section is a tempo change (82 to 62), not a modulation the parts imply. None is a cross-rhythm or hemiola.

voice_language.hihat: Eighths, the hat open or half-open on the 'and' of 4; sixteenths in Paranoid Android's slow section.
voice_language.snare: The cross-stick often in place of the snare; the snare pushed off the backbeat (Just); stuttering round 2 and 3 (15 Step).
voice_language.kick: 1, the 'a' of 2 and the 'and' of 3 (Creep); on every 'and' (Bodysnatchers).
voice_language.toms: The floor tom as the time (There There, Bodysnatchers); runs round the toms into a section.
voice_language.cymbals: The ride for the chorus, its bell on the off-beats (Just, Reckoner).

aesthetic: a different sound for each song: 'The sound of the drums has to be right for each song'
sound_profile.cymbal_character: Plain crashes and a ride used for its bell.

sample_hints.alternative-rock: A tight, dry studio rock kit; a big room for Creep and There There; damped drums for Karma Police; a small, lo-fi kit for 15 Step.

signature_traits.label: The cross-stick in place of the snare
signature_traits.description: Paranoid Android's 'restrained cross-sticking' twice on 2 and on 4; There There's cross-stick under the floor tom; Creep's last chorus.

signature_traits.label: A part for each song
signature_traits.description: Each song its own figure, held: Creep's kick, There There's toms, Bodysnatchers' off-beat kick, 15 Step's stutter; 'none of those styles is a carbon copy'.

patterns.name: Creep: the kick on 1, the 'a' of 2 and the 'and' of 3
patterns.function: The verse: eighths on the hat, half-open on the 'and' of 4 every other bar, the snare on 2 and 4.

patterns.name: Paranoid Android: the cross-stick twice on 2 and on 4
patterns.function: The first section's bar: eighths on the hat, the cross-stick on 2 and its 'e' and on 4 and its 'e', the kick on 1, its 'e' and 'and', the 'a' of 2, the 'e' of 3 and the 'and' of 3.

evidence.note: Rhythm (2001) on his 'restrained cross-sticking for much of the first three minutes'.

patterns.name: There There: the floor tom in eighths
patterns.function: The floor tom in eighths, the cross-stick on 2 and 4, the high tom on the 'and' of 2, the low tom on the 'and' of 4, the kick on 1 and the 'and' of 3, the hat's foot on the beat.

patterns.name: Reckoner: ghost notes round the ride
patterns.function: The ride in eighths, the snare on 2 and 4 with ghosts on the 'e' of 1, the 'a' of 2, the 'e' of 3 and the 'a' of 4; the kick on the 'and' of 1 and of 3.

patterns.name: 15 Step: his kit in 5/4
patterns.function: A bar of 5/4 as the tab writes it: eighths on the hat, the kick on 1, the 'a' and 'and' of 2 and the 'and' of 3, then again; the snare's rimshots and hits stuttering round 2 and 3 and 4 and 5.

evidence.note: Played over the record's programmed pattern.

patterns.name: Bodysnatchers: the kick on every 'and'
patterns.function: The ride in eighths, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on the 'and' of every beat, the hat's foot on the beat.

evidence.note: 'I think I have borrowed quite a bit from Stephen Morris's drumming over the years.'
He called Blondie's Clem Burke his 'drummer hero'.
Radiohead's second drummer on the King of Limbs and Moon Shaped Pool tours: 'One played in the traditional way, the other almost mimicked a drum machine.'
Mojo: 'surely the most inventive rhythm section working close to the rock mainstream'.

innovations: Playing machine parts on the kit: Idioteque live, 15 Step
Cross-stick and toms as the groove in a rock band (Paranoid Android, There There)

accolades.title: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, with Radiohead

common_misconceptions: That every drum on the records is his playing: Airbag is a loop cut from his drums, Idioteque has 'no real drums', and 15 Step layers his kit over a machine.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A tight, dry studio rock kit; a big room for Creep and There There, damped drums for Karma Police, a small lo-fi kit for 15 Step
generation_rules: One figure held per section, as the record holds it.
The cross-stick or the toms in place of the snare where the song is quiet.
Few fills; a run round the toms at a section change.
Straight time, no swing; odd meters where the song has them.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Joy Division's Stephen Morris, by his own account, and Blondie's Clem Burke, his 'drummer hero': Radiohead's parts-first drummer.
